newsitem.title: UK: IRAQ PICTURE CLEARS, MED URALS CRUDE REPRIEVED.
newsitem.headline: IRAQ PICTURE CLEARS, MED URALS CRUDE REPRIEVED.

text.p: Iraqi barrels were being quietly offered on the spot market on Monday as loading programmes for resumed exports firmed up, traders said.

But prices were not discussed and little of the first 10 days of loading at the Turkish port of Ceyhan was being shown with much conviction, giving Russian Urals, the alternative regional sour, a temporary reprieve.
"There are quite a few people showing barrels but we're not seeing numbers yet, they're just testing the market," said a trader with a potential Kirkuk buyer in Europe.

Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said he anticipated 30 million barrels of oil being exported by the end of August, with the first two million barrel shipment from Ceyhan in the next two days.

Rasheed said the tanker Arcadia anchored at Ceyhan on Monday and was awaiting approval of contracts by U.N. overseers before beginning to load. Shipping brokers said the VLCC was chartered by U.S. firm Bayoil.
A provisional loading schedule for liftings from Ceyhan was available from industry sources by mid-afternoon, indicating exports at a rate of 875,000 barrels per day.

That would leave Iraq planning to move 625,000 bpd from its Gulf port of Mina al-Bakr if it is to match Rasheed's figure and come anywhere close to its ambitious cash target of $1 billion worth of exports by September 5.
That compares with just over 650,000 bpd total from both ports during the first six months of the U.N.'s oil-for-food deal.
With heavy volumes of Iraqi oil hitting world markets over the next three weeks Urals' discount to dated Brent was expected to slump towards the $1.20 to $1.30 level by September.
